content.text: Only Section 6.11 grants Harpoon an audit right against AbbVie. Its material terms match the preferred position, with parameters redacted.

input.quote: 6.11 Audit. AbbVie shall, shall cause its Affiliates to, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cause its Sublicensees to, keep complete and accurate books and records pertaining to Net Sales of Licensed Products, in sufficient detail to calculate all amounts payable hereunder. At the request of Harpoon, AbbVie shall permit an independent public accounting firm of nationally recognized standing designated by Harpoon and reasonably acceptable to AbbVie, [***], to audit the books and records maintained pursuant to this Section 6.11
input.rationale: Section 6.11 is the only audit right binding us (AbbVie). It meets the preferred position on each material term: the audit is limited to royalty books and records (no access to our systems); it must be conducted by an independent public accounting firm of nationally recognized standing designated by Harpoon but reasonably acceptable to us; frequency is capped at not more than once in any stated period, with look-back and repeat-period limits; the auditor may report only whether reports are correct and the details of discrepancies, with no other information shared; Harpoon bears the cost unless the audit reveals a variance above the stated threshold; and Section 6.13 plus Article 9 impose confidentiality on the reviewing firm/Audit Expert. Section 6.12 allocates dispute costs neutrally via the Audit Expert. The frequency period, timing qualifier and variance percentage are redacted as [***], and no numeric advance-notice period is spelled out on the face of the clause (audits occur "at the request of Harpoon" and the redaction likely carries a reasonable-notice/business-hours qualifier) — we note these as points to confirm against the unredacted figures (frequency once per 12 months, notice of 15–30 days, variance threshold no lower than 5%), but they are sub-parameters rather than material failures. No unlimited, unannounced or remote-access audit rights exist, so nothing approaches walk-away territory and no redline is warranted.
